source.note: Healey & Picard, IEEE T-ITS 2005 · PhysioNet. ECG and EMG only, from Hans's ECG dashboard export.

modalities.label: ECG
modalities.detail: Chest ECG, modified lead II, 248 Hz

quality.message: Signal looks clean enough for HRV analysis.

fusion.title: Stress response
fusion.method: Decision-level fusion of ECG and EMG · each signal votes on whether it moved the way stress predicts
fusion.note: 3 of 3 signals across ECG and EMG shifted toward stress between rest and city driving — two modalities agreeing is what makes it credible.

findings.label: Healthy heart-rate variability
findings.detail: RMSSD 63 ms at rest (below 20 ms is low)

findings.label: Acute stress response while driving
findings.detail: Heart rate +24 bpm, HRV -50%, muscle tension ×25 — the normal reaction to city traffic, not a disorder

advice.text: No need to contact a doctor — the resting readings are within normal ranges.

assessment.disclaimer: Screening aid, not a diagnosis. Heart rate uses the standard adult resting range (50–100 bpm); a camera reading outside it asks for a rescan before any doctor visit.

pipeline.detail: 74400 ECG samples at 248 Hz with R-peaks from Hans's pipeline
Filtered ECG mean-pooled from 248 to 62 Hz for display — QRS complexes stay visible
Valid R-R intervals converted to bpm and interpolated onto an even 2 Hz grid
EMG rectified and averaged from 15.5 Hz onto the same 2 Hz grid
Heart rate, HRV and muscle tension compared with the direction stress predicts
